ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a triangular/checkerboard-like arrangement of alternating light and dark squares. At the top there is a visible stack of four horizontal alternating rows, each beginning and ending with a dark square. There is also a visible bottom horizontal alternating row, again beginning and ending with a dark square. Between the upper stack and the bottom row, the middle is left blank with the printed words “same pattern here,” and along each sloping side there are three isolated dark squares. Reasoning: Use cancellation. In any visible horizontal alternating row that starts and ends with a dark square, adjacent dark-light pairs cancel, leaving 1 extra dark square. The four upper rows therefore contribute 4 extra dark squares. The bottom row contributes 1 extra dark square. The three isolated dark squares on the left side and the three isolated dark squares on the right side are not paired in those row cancellations, so they contribute 6 more extra dark squares. Total excess dark squares = 4 + 1 + 6 = 11.

In each visible horizontal alternating row that starts and ends with a dark square, pair off adjacent dark-light squares; each such row contributes one extra dark square. The four upper rows contribute 4 extra dark squares, and the bottom row contributes 1 extra dark square. The three isolated sloping-side dark squares on the left and the three on the right are not paired with light squares in those horizontal-row cancellations, so they contribute 6 more extra dark squares. Add the remaining extras: 4 + 1 + 6 = 11.
